title: The proper-image reduction tower of open extension equals the compact-support tower
statement: Let $K_0$ be a field, $X,Y$ finite-type $K_0$-schemes, $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism, and $c=(X\xrightarrow j V\xrightarrow p Y)$ a compactification [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Assume $j$ is quasi-compact. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$, a uniformizer $t$ and $P_n=A/t^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale sites put $R_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$, and let $\operatorname{Res}_n$ be restriction along $R_W\to(P_n)_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars]. Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], put $L=j_!K$ using completed ringed extension by zero [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], and let $K_n,L_n$ be their derived finite reductions [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Let $\alpha_n:L_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!K_n$ be the evaluated canonical comparison of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Set $N_n=\operatorname{Res}_n Rp_{*,n}L_n$ and $M_n=\operatorname{Res}_n Rf^c_{!,n}K_n$, where $Rp_{*,n}$ is the ordinary finite-coefficient derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and $Rf^c_{!,n}=Rp_{*,n}j_!$ is the same finite composite as in [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Put $S_n=\operatorname{Res}^{P_{n+1}}_{P_n}$, let $d_n:L_{n+1}\to S_nL_n$ be the quotient reduction, and let $C_n(H):Rp_{*,n+1}S_nH\xrightarrow{\sim}S_nRp_{*,n}H$ be [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]. Equip $N_\bullet$ with the transitions $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(C_n(L_n)\circ Rp_{*,n+1}(d_n))$, and equip $M_\bullet$ with the transitions obtained by applying $Rf^c_{!,n+1}$ to $K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}^{P_{n+1}}_{P_n}K_n$ and then the comparison of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars], followed by restriction to $R_Y$. Then $\beta_n=\operatorname{Res}_n Rp_{*,n}(\alpha_n):N_n\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n$ is an isomorphism of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system]: $\beta_n t^N_n=t^M_n\beta_{n+1}$ for every $n\geq1$. No constructibility or Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $K$ is required.

proof.text:
Write $D_n=Rp_{*,n}$ and $J_n=j_!$ at coefficient level $P_n$, and distinguish $S_n^X,S_n^V,S_n^Y$ when necessary. Let $k_n:K_{n+1}\to S_n^XK_n$ be quotient reduction. The strict-system assertion of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison], evaluated at the consecutive quotient, gives
$$S_n^V(\alpha_n)\circ d_n=e_n(K_n)\circ J_{n+1}(k_n)\circ\alpha_{n+1},$$
where $e_n:J_{n+1}S_n^X\xrightarrow{\sim}S_n^VJ_n$ is the open-extension/scalar-restriction identification specified in [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. These are the same open identifications: both act as the identity on the underlying open sections with the quotient scalar action. Thus the displayed equation uses the canonical $\alpha_n$ and actual quotient maps, rather than arbitrarily chosen levelwise isomorphisms. The open-comparison hypotheses hold because $j$ is quasi-compact, $K$ is derived complete, and $\ell$ is invertible on all the schemes over $K_0$.

proof.text:
Put $b_n=D_n(\alpha_n)$, $u_n=C_n(L_n)\circ D_{n+1}(d_n)$, and
$$v_n=C_n(J_nK_n)\circ D_{n+1}(e_n(K_n))\circ D_{n+1}(J_{n+1}(k_n)).$$
By the formula specifying the comparison in [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars], $v_n$ is exactly the compact-support transition before restriction to $R_Y$; $u_n$ is the proper-image transition in the statement. The application uses the given separated finite-type $f$, its same compactification $c$, and the quotient homomorphism $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ of finite commutative rings. Finiteness and these quotient maps are part of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Hence $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}u_n=t_n^N$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}v_n=t_n^M$, with the specified scalar-restriction identifications at their targets.

source.place: Integral compact-support formula: the finite-level quotient transitions, expanded by the defining composite in the scalar-restriction theorem

proof.text:
Naturality in the argument of $C_n$ from [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars], applied to $\alpha_n:L_n\to J_nK_n$, says
$$S_n^Y(b_n)\circ C_n(L_n)=C_n(J_nK_n)\circ D_{n+1}(S_n^V(\alpha_n)).$$
Compose with $D_{n+1}(d_n)$ and substitute Step 1. Functoriality of $D_{n+1}$ gives the entire transition calculation:
$$\begin{aligned}
S_n^Y(b_n)\circ u_n
&=C_n(J_nK_n)\circ D_{n+1}(S_n^V(\alpha_n)\circ d_n)\\
&=C_n(J_nK_n)\circ D_{n+1}(e_n(K_n))\circ D_{n+1}(J_{n+1}(k_n))\circ D_{n+1}(\alpha_{n+1})\\
&=v_n\circ b_{n+1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The direct-image theorem allows every scheme morphism and these finite coefficient rings, so it applies to $p$ without any bound or constructibility condition on its arguments.

source.place: Integral compact-support formula: agent-written naturality calculation for its consecutive quotient transitions

proof.text: Restriction of scalars is termwise as in [def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars]. The equality $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}S_n^Y=\operatorname{Res}_n$ holds on objects and arrows: for $a\in R_Y$ both actions are multiplication by its image in $(P_n)_Y$. Applying $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}$ to Step 3 therefore gives $\beta_n\circ t_n^N=t_n^M\circ\beta_{n+1}$. Each $\beta_n$ is invertible, since functors carry the inverse of $\alpha_n$ to an inverse. The consecutive equations are precisely a morphism of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system], and their composites give the equations for every $m\ge n$. Composing the consecutive equation with the component inverses gives $t_n^N\circ\beta_{n+1}^{-1}=\beta_n^{-1}\circ t_n^M$. Thus the component inverses also form a system morphism, whose two composites with $\beta$ are the identity componentwise. This proves the claimed system isomorphism. Every input used above holds for the arbitrary derived-complete $K$ of the statement.
